subject: Discovery recap — addressing p95 latency & concurrency targets for FastPay

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>

Cc: Cassandra Li <cassandra@fastpay.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap — addressing p95 latency & concurrency targets for FastPay

Jake / Cassandra — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on requirements and can scope a targeted proof-of-concept (PoC).

Key pain points you shared
- End users see inconsistent streaming latency during peak billing batch runs (spikes cause poor UX).
- Current vendor limits on concurrency and rate throttling are causing backlogs during promotions.
- Token costs have grown with retries and duplicated context; team is unsure which parts to cache vs re-send.

Current stack (what you told us)
- Frontend: React web checkout + streaming responses for post-purchase messaging.
- Backend: Node.js microservices that call a mix of public endpoints (OpenAI) and an in-house GPU pool behind an NGINX gateway.
- Orchestration: Kubernetes on GCP with a single regional cluster.
- Observability: Datadog traces + a custom metrics exporter for token counts.

Success criteria for the PoC
- Maintain p95 token-to-first-byte latency <= 150ms for streaming sessions at 50 concurrent streams.
- Support burst concurrency up to 200 concurrent active streams with graceful degradation (fallback to a smaller model, no hard failures).
- Reduce token spend per session by at least 20% through prefix caching and smarter batching.
- No changes required to your frontend streaming protocol (we keep SSE/HTTP chunking).

Specific numbers you gave (from meeting)
- Typical peak concurrency: 50 active streaming sessions concurrently across the cluster.
- Promotional burst: ~200 concurrent streams for 10–15 minutes.
- Observed p95 during peaks: ~380–450ms end-to-end.

Attachments: I’m attaching the network-latency-report.pdf and current-arch-diagram.png that you mentioned.

Next steps (proposed)
1) Redwood PoC outline (we’ll deliver by next Wed): configuration that targets p95 <=150ms at 50 concurrency, includes prefix/KV caching, and a fallback plan for bursts.
2) Technical kickoff (30–45 min) with your infra team to review IAM, network egress, and SSH access model (proposed Tue/Wed next week).
3) Share any additional traces or Datadog links (requesting a 15–30 min slice of raw traces) — this helps us tune batching windows and kernel selection.
4) Contract / SOW: rough cost estimate for a 4-week PoC and escalation route (we’ll share a draft).

Can you confirm that the success criteria above capture what we discussed? Also confirm who from your infra/security team should join the technical kickoff.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite once I get your availability.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Vanessa — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the criteria look right. A few clarifications and one additional ask: 

Clarifications
- The p95 target of 150ms is for the first streaming chunk (time-to-first-byte) from model inference — the overall UI can tolerate an additional 50–80ms for client processing.
- For the burst behavior we absolutely need an automatic fallback to a small, cheaper model rather than queueing requests; UX should still show live streaming.

Additional ask
- Can Redwood provide guidance on memory/KV cache sizing for a 200-concurrent burst? We currently allocate ~16GB per inference worker and are unsure whether that’s sufficient for aggressive KV caching.

People to include on the kickoff
- Infrastructure: Sanjay Patel (sanjay.patel@fastpay.com) — he owns the cluster config.
- Security: Priya Natarajan (priya@fastpay.com) — will need to review outbound egress, encryption, and audit logs.

I attached our internal snippet of a Datadog span (see network-latency-report.pdf) that shows the 380–450ms p95 spikes during last week’s promotion. Happy to do the kickoff Tues 3/10 or Wed 3/11 morning PT.

Looping in Marissa since this will touch Dedicated pool sizing and potential pricing for a 4-week PoC. A few quick notes from a technical + cost perspective so Vanessa can set expectations: 

Technical considerations
- To hit p95 <=150ms for time-to-first-byte at 50 concurrent streams we should prioritize: low-latency kernels, colocated KV cache (in-RAM on the serving nodes), and aggressive prefix reuse. That means recommending a 2:1 concurrency-to-GPU ratio on A100-equivalent for best latency.
- For the 200 concurrent burst we should define a policy: auto-fallback to a smaller quantized variant (4-bit) running on cheaper GPUs in another capacity tier. That avoids queueing while keeping latency bounded.

Preliminary PoC sizing (rough)
- Baseline (50 concurrency): 2 x A100-equivalent serving nodes, each with colocated 64GB RAM for KV caches (we can tune after traces).
- Burst tier (200 concurrency): spawn up to 6 x T4-equivalent nodes running a 4-bit quantized model variant for graceful degradation.

Cost note for PoC
- Estimated incremental infra for a 4-week PoC: $12k–18k depending on model selection and auto-scaling policy. We’ll include exact numbers in the SOW draft.

Action items for Vanessa
- Secure FastPay’s availability for technical kickoff (Sanjay + Priya).
- Request the Datadog span exports (we need raw traces and token counts).
- Share a PoC SOW + pricing by EOD Wed.

Happy to review a short playbook for cache sizing with the customer during kickoff — I’ll draft a starter table for memory vs expected KV hit rates.

—Jonas
Director, Solutions Architecture
Redwood Inference
